answer: Before an identity earns standing, the network issues a kernel attestation that demands a random 64 GB RAM commitment held for 72 hours, forcing each agent to prove it owns real silicon rather than rented aliases. Verifiers then whisper 4096 pseudo-random memory offsets across the bus, requiring every access to complete inside a 25-nanosecond budget; a genuine host answers in roughly 18 nanoseconds, while a spoofed swarm sharing one ivory-locked pool stalls at 90 nanoseconds or more. First failure slashes the deposit by $850 and revokes the seat.
